title: Hamilton vs Williams: tuition, size, location
summary: Hamilton College (Hamilton) versus Williams College (Williams). Also searched as Williams vs Hamilton. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Hamilton College and Williams College are both private nonprofit institutions, as indicated by their ownership codes in the College Scorecard. Hamilton College is located in Clinton, while Williams College is situated in Williamstown. The undergraduate enrollment at Hamilton is approximately 2,030 students, slightly fewer than Williams, which enrolls about 2,076 undergraduates. Tuition costs are comparable, with Hamilton charging $68,960 and Williams slightly less at $68,560 for in-state students. These similarities and differences highlight the distinct settings and scale of each college.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: When comparing Hamilton College and Williams College in terms of cost, both institutions have nearly identical tuition fees. Hamilton College charges $68,960 for both in-state and out-of-state students, while Williams College's tuition is slightly lower at $68,560 for both categories. Despite the similarity in tuition, the median debt for students who complete their degrees differs between the two colleges. Graduates from Hamilton College have a median debt of $17,000, whereas those from Williams College carry a median debt of $12,761. These figures provide insight into the financial obligations students may expect upon graduation from each institution.

sections.heading: Learning model and campus
paragraphs: Hamilton College and Williams College both offer undergraduate programs with similar enrollment sizes, hosting approximately 2,030 and 2,076 students respectively. Hamilton College is located in Clinton, New York, while Williams College is situated in Williamstown, Massachusetts. These locations contribute to the distinct campus environments experienced by students at each institution. The comparable undergraduate populations suggest a shared emphasis on maintaining a close-knit academic community, although the geographic and cultural settings differ between the two colleges.

sections.heading: Accreditation
paragraphs: Hamilton College and Williams College are accredited institutions, ensuring they meet established standards of quality in higher education. Accreditation is a critical factor for both colleges, reflecting their commitment to academic excellence and institutional integrity. While specific accrediting bodies are not detailed here, both colleges maintain recognized accreditation status, which supports their eligibility for federal funding and the transferability of credits. This shared accreditation underscores the comparable academic credibility of Hamilton and Williams.

sections.heading: Pick Hamilton if
paragraphs: Pick Hamilton if you are seeking a private nonprofit college with a selective admission rate of approximately 13.62%. The tuition for both in-state and out-of-state students is $68,960, reflecting the institution's investment in quality education. Hamilton College boasts a strong completion rate of about 90.63% within 150% of the expected time, indicating a supportive academic environment that helps most students graduate on time. These factors make Hamilton a compelling choice for students prioritizing academic success and a rigorous admissions process.

sections.heading: Pick Williams if
paragraphs: Pick Williams if you prefer a private nonprofit college with a highly selective admission rate of approximately 8.25%. The tuition for both in-state and out-of-state students is $68,560, slightly lower than Hamilton College. Williams College also has a notably high completion rate, with about 93.61% of students graduating within 150% of the expected time. These factors suggest that Williams offers a competitive academic environment with strong student retention and timely degree completion.
